As a software developer and a musician, I've always been interested in ways I could utilize both skillsets into making music. There's actually a lot of interesting overlap between programming and music. Granted that music can vary wildly in its structure and form, music is usually broken down into multiple sections such as intro, verse, chorus, bridge, etc... Those sections are then made up of harmonies, which are made with rhythms and melodies, which are themselves made up of notes and instruments playing those notes. The point is that music can be made with various building blocks that can be combined and arranged in various ways to create music.

In a similar fashion, software can be organized into various reusable components that can be combined to create various features.

In music, often times you have various parts that repeat over and over and are combined with other various parts. So, what if you could utilize the expressiveness of programming to break music down into various parts and reuse them using functions and variables?

# Strudel
Strudel allows you to expressively write music and is a Javascript port of the Tidal Cycles. It allows you to make music with code in real time!

Lets start building a song. Firstly, we'll start with a beat.
<script src="https://unpkg.com/@strudel/embed@latest"></script>
<strudel-repl>
<!--
$: s("hh!8").gain(.2)
$: s("bd").beat("0,7,10", 16).gain(.5)
$: s("sd").beat("4,12",16).gain(.3)
-->
</strudel-repl>
Let's break this down:

- `s()` is a function that takes a sound. In this case, we are using hihat (hh), bass drum (bd), and snare drum (sd).
- In the first line, we added `!8`. This means that the hihat will play 8 times during the cycle. You can think of cycles like measures in music. We also use the gain function to reduce the volume.
- In the second line, we use the beat function to define when the bass drum gets hit. We are hitting the bass drum on beat 0, 7, and 10 out of 16 beats per cycle.

Lets vary the beat a bit:
<strudel-repl>
<!--
$: s("hh!8").gain(.2)
$: s("bd").beat("0,<7.1 8>,10.2", 16).gain(.5)
$: s("sd").beat("4,12,<~ ~ ~ 14>",16).gain(.3)
-->
</strudel-repl>

With the use of `<>` , we can now change when the sound is played per cycle. We're also using decimals to offset the beats by just a small amount to make it sound less robotic.

The `~` symbol stands for rest, meaning no sound is played for the first 3 cycles.

Now lets play some notes:
<strudel-repl>
<!--
$: s("hh!8").gain(.2)
$: s("bd").beat("0,<7.1 8>,10.2", 16).gain(.5)
$: s("sd").beat("4,12,<~ ~ ~ 14>",16).gain(.3)
$: note("<f#3 g#3 a#3 g#3>").s("piano")
-->
</strudel-repl>

We are using `<>` again so that one note is played per cycle. If we remove the brackets, then each note will be played once per cycle as quarter notes. Notice that there are no this time. the `note()` function treats commas as notes that should be played together, so lets use that to make chords:

<strudel-repl>
<!--
$: s("hh!8").gain(.2)
$: s("bd").beat("0,<7.1 8>,10.2", 16).gain(.5)
$: s("sd").beat("4,12,<~ ~ ~ 14>",16).gain(.3)
$: note("<[f#3,a#3] [g#3,c4] [a#3,c#4] [g#3,c4]>").s("piano")
-->
</strudel-repl>

It can be difficult to remember and type out the notes, so lets refactor and use scale instead:

<strudel-repl>
<!--
$: s("hh!8").gain(.2)
$: s("bd").beat("0,<7.1 8>,10.2", 16).gain(.5)
$: s("sd").beat("4,12,<~ ~ ~ 14>",16).gain(.3)
$: n(`<[-2,2] [-1,3] [0,4] [-1,3]>`).scale("A#3:minor").s("piano")
-->
</strudel-repl>

Now we can just use the numbers on the scale rather than having to try and remember the key. It also means we can switch our song between different keys.

In fact, we use the same notation to change the scale after each note is played!

<strudel-repl>
<!--
$: s("hh!8").gain(.2)
$: s("bd").beat("0,<7.1 8>,10.2", 16).gain(.5)
$: s("sd").beat("4,12,<~ ~ ~ 14>",16).gain(.3)
$: n(`<[-2,2]*2 [-1,3]*2 [0,4]*2 [-1,3]*2>`).scale("[A#3:minor A#2:minor]").s("piano")
-->
</strudel-repl>

We are now using `*2` to play each chord twice each cycle and each time we are changing the octaves.

Because this is javascript, we can also use variables to reuse beats:

<strudel-repl>
<!--
const hihat = s("hh!8").gain(.2)
const bass = s("bd").beat("0,<7.1 8>,10.2", 16).gain(.5)
const snare = s("sd").beat("4,12,<~ ~ ~ 14>",16).gain(.3)
const chords = n(`<[-2,2]*2 [-1,3]*2 [0,4]*2 [-1,3]*2>`).scale("[A#3:minor A#2:minor]").s("piano")
$: arrange(
  [8, stack(hihat, bass, snare)], //Introduction
  [8, stack(hihat, bass, snare, chords)], //Adds Chords
)._pianoroll()
-->
</strudel-repl>

Now we are using `arrange()` to create parts of our songs using our different pieces. `stack()` allows us to play various parts together to make different sounds. With that, you basically have everything you need to start making music!

Here you can see a full song I made:
<strudel-repl>
<!--

setCps(140/60/4)
//$: s("breaks/2").fit().orbit(2)

const dbbank = "tr909"

let hihat = s("hh!8").decay(.4).gain(.2).sometimesBy(.1, x => x.ply("2 | 4"))._punchcard()


let bass = s("bd").beat("0,<7.1 8>,10.2", 16).gain(.5).bank(dbbank).duck("2:3:4").duckattack(.2).duckdepth(.8)._punchcard()
let snare =  s("sd").bank(dbbank).beat("4,12,<~ ~ ~ 14>",16).distort(2).gain(.2).room(.5)._punchcard()

 

function xylo(notes){
  return notes.distort(2)
  //.lpf(4000)
  //.lpenv(4)
  //.velocity("1 2")
  .gain(".3")
  .delay(.3)
    .ph(saw.slow(2).range(1,4))
    .lpf(saw.slow(2).range(500,1000))
    .lpenv(saw.slow(.15).range(1,4))
    //.compressor("-20:5:10:.002:.02")
  .s("sawtooth")
  //.s("xylophone_soft_ff")
}

let chords = n(`<[-2,2] [-1,3] [0,4] [-1,3]>`).scale("A#2:minor")._pianoroll()

let melody1 = xylo(n(`<-2 -1 0 -1> 2 1 2 <6 6 6 3> 2 1 2`)).scale("A#3:minor")._pianoroll()

let bridge = xylo(n(`[0 1 2 <[1 [2 -1]] [4 3 2 1]>]/4`).scale("A#3:minor"))._pianoroll()

let bridge2 = xylo(n(`[[0 1]@1.5 0@0.5 [1 2]@1.5 1@0.5 [2 3]@1.5 2@0.5 [1 2]@1.5 [-1 0]@0.5]/4`).scale("A#3:minor"))._pianoroll()

let breakdown = xylo(n(`[6 5 4 3 2 1 2 3]/4`).scale("A#3:minor"))._pianoroll()

let breakdown2 = xylo(n(`[[6 5]@1.5 4@0.5 [5 4]@1.5 3@0.5 [2 2]@1.5 3@0.5 [1 1]@1.5 2@0.5]/4`).scale("A#3:minor"))._pianoroll()

let melody2 = xylo(n(`<-2 -1 0 3> 2 1 2`).scale("A#3:minor"))._pianoroll()

let bassSynth = n(irand(10).sub(7).seg(8))
  .scale("A#2:minor")
  .rib(0, 2)
  .s("supersaw")
  .lpf(200)
  .lpenv(saw.range(1, 2))
  .lpq(12)
  .orbit(2)
  .delay(.5)

$: arrange(
  [4, stack(bassSynth, hihat, bass, snare)],
  [4, stack(bassSynth, hihat, bass, snare, chords)],
  [8, stack(bassSynth, hihat, bass, snare, chords, bridge)],
  [8, stack(bassSynth, hihat, bass, snare, chords, bridge2)],
  [8, stack(bassSynth, hihat, bass, snare, chords, melody1)],
  [4, stack(bassSynth, hihat, bass, snare, chords, breakdown)],
  [4, stack(bassSynth, hihat, bass, snare, chords, breakdown2)],
  [8, stack(bassSynth, hihat, bass, snare, chords, melody1)],
  [0.5, n(`~`)],
  [8, stack(bassSynth, hihat, bass, snare, chords, melody2)],
  [4, stack(bassSynth, hihat, bass, snare, chords, breakdown)],
  [4, stack(bassSynth, hihat, bass, snare, chords, breakdown2)],
  [8, stack(bassSynth, hihat, bass, snare, chords, melody1)],
)._pianoroll()._scope()
-->
</strudel-repl>
